name: NY-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+24 partisan lean in a heavily Democratic Queens-based seat
Meeks holds about $2.1 million on hand versus no reported challenger fundraising
Long-tenured incumbent with no polls or expert ratings indicating vulnerability
Prediction markets price Democratic retention near 98 percent
model.rationale: The district's 24-point Democratic lean, Meeks's large financial edge, and markets pricing retention near 98 percent point to an easy Democratic hold, and nothing in the record suggests the challenger has the resources to test it.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for Marsh or an unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would require a shift far beyond anything seen here.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New York's fifth district, centered in Queens, is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country. Representative Gregory Meeks, first elected in 1998, is seeking another term with the advantages of incumbency, seniority, and a large financial edge. He has raised about $2.2 million and holds roughly $2.1 million on hand, while Republican George Marsh shows no reported fundraising.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals. The seat's 24-point Democratic lean, combined with Meeks's resources and name recognition, makes an upset highly unlikely. Prediction markets price Democratic retention near 98 percent. The main question is the size of Meeks's victory margin, not which party carries the district.
